case_title.reason: Title matches the judgment caption: Jagjit Singh v. State of Punjab.

number_of_accused.reason: The appeal is by the appellant alone; he was tried with parents and brothers, but only his liability is decided here.

accused_gender.reason: The accused is the victim's husband and the appellant; male is supported.

accused_age.reason: No age of the appellant is stated in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: No religious identity of the accused is described in the judgment.

accused_caste.reason: No caste or community of the accused is named.

accused_occupation.reason: Only an uncertain witness reply about turner work appears; no occupation is established, so Not stated is defensible.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Judgment records the accused's Rs.3000 monthly earnings and DW8's account of an average family versus a well-off PW3 family.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No prior criminal record is mentioned.

victim_gender.reason: The victim is the appellant's wife, referred to as a woman who died with her child.

victim_age.reason: The victim's age is not stated.

victim_caste.reason: No caste or community of the victim is named.

victim_religion.reason: No religious identity of the victim is described.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: The accused was the victim's husband; spouse is supported.

offence_category.reason: The conviction is under IPC s.304-B for dowry death.

statutory_provisions.reason: Judgment cites s.304-B IPC, s.113-B Evidence Act, s.406 IPC and s.498-A IPC as referenced in the trial.

weapon.reason: Death was by drowning; no weapon is mentioned.

evidence_type.reason: Oral testimony, post-mortem opinion and circumstantial proximity evidence are all discussed.

confession.reason: No confession or admission by the accused is mentioned.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Alleged beatings, taunts, expulsion and the conditional 'if believed' beating are noted in the judgment.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: Court notes the appellant's father funded education and that the father-in-law was acquitted at trial.

trial_court_outcome.reason: Trial court convicted under s.304-B, sentenced to 8 years RI, acquitted under s.406; no separate s.498-A conviction.

high_court_outcome.reason: High Court affirmed conviction under s.304-B and reduced sentence from 8 to 7 years.

final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, so the conviction stands.

offence_finally_established.reason: Conviction under IPC s.304-B stands after dismissal of the appeal.

imprisonment_type.reason: Sentence is a fixed term of rigorous imprisonment.

imprisonment_years.reason: High Court reduced the sentence to 7 years, which the Supreme Court left in place.

fine_rs.reason: No fine is mentioned in the judgment.

neutral_facts.reason: Facts track the prosecution evidence without names or outcome; no court proceedings or verdict are revealed; length is within limits.

offence_severity.reason: The judgment does not state the statutory maximum or minimum for s.304-B.

attempt_completion.reason: The death occurred, so the offence is completed.

physical_harm.reason: Death of the victim and her child by drowning is recorded.

number_of_offences.reason: Three sections (s.304-B, s.406, s.498-A) are referenced in the trial; only s.304-B conviction is upheld.

financial_property_loss.reason: No property or money was lost as a result of the offence.

premeditation_planning.reason: The judgment does not discuss premeditation or planning.

motive.correct_value: alleged: demand for a Maruti car or Rs.2 lakh as dowry; the court treated it as dowry-related cruelty only if the testimony is believed
motive.quote: If he is to be believed (In fact, two courts have), this would amount to cruelty/harassment in connection with demand for dowry.
motive.reason: The court did not decide the motive; it was conditional on belief, so it should be marked as alleged.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: Court relied on PW1 and PW3 testimony, PW4/PW5 evidence on weeping at PCO, and the post-mortem timing opinion.

witness_credibility.quote: If he is to be believed (In fact, two courts have)
witness_credibility.reason: Credibility was not reappraised; trial court's demeanour advantage was noted and its view affirmed, as stated.

post_offence_conduct.reason: No post-offence conduct of the accused such as absconding or disclosure is recorded by the court.

trial_duration.reason: Offence date, High Court date (27.02.2015) and Supreme Court date (26.09.2018) match; trial judgment date not given.

legal_representation.reason: Counsel for appellant and State match the judgment's listing.

investigation_status.reason: FIR on 17.02.2001 and post-mortem on 28.02.2001 are stated; charge sheet date not given.

procedural_irregularity.reason: The court notes no procedural lapse; the unexamined witness Avtar Singh is a evidentiary gap, not an irregularity.

appeal_history.reason: Trial conviction, High Court reduction to 7 years and Supreme Court dismissal are accurately summarised.

prosecution_argument.reason: State argued defence neighbours DW6 and DW8 are unreliable and PW1/PW3 show temporal proximity.

defence_argument.reason: Defence contended no cruelty or dowry demand, sister's taunting, and family financing of the victim's education, as stated.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Limits on Art.136 interference, the rebuttable s.113-B presumption and the relative meaning of 'soon before' are all applied.

precedent_relied_upon.reason: Relied-on and referred cases match the judgment's citations, including Ganga Kumar via Mohd. Ali.

sentencing_rationale.reason: The Supreme Court gave no sentencing reasoning; it only dismissed the appeal.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: The court did not weigh mitigating factors for sentence; the father's education funding was listed only as a troubling feature.

judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: If this be true, indeed, it is cruelty near, in point of time and bearing a link proximate to the time of her death
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court itself weighed the proximity of the alleged previous-night cruelty to death, conditionally, as stated.

other_sentence_order.reason: No compensation, directions or guidelines are ordered.
